text:
maria: Heads-up: multiple customers reporting elevated p95/p99 in eu-west starting ~08:10 UTC. Support ticket stream + alerts showing TLS handshake times spiking to 2-4s, overall request latency up ~3x. Repro from curl shows long TCP->TLS time.

jonah: seeing same in dashboards. p95 went 180ms->900ms, p99 ~4s. Top affected routes look like anycast to eu-west POPs E1/E3.

eli: I pulled histograms — spike correlates with increased retransmits and SYN retransmits between our POPs and some upstreams. No recent deploys in control plane at 08:10.

maria: @net-bot can you post recent BGP session flaps for eu-west?

net-bot: BGP alerts: session 10.2.4.5 <-> rr-eu-west-1 flapped 08:09:42 -> 08:15:11 (6 mins). Affected prefixes: 203.0.113.0/24, 198.51.100.0/24.

jonah: interesting — anycast weight shift or upstream partner maintenance?

eli: partner NOC says they had a short maintenance but denied impact. I'll traceroute a failing request from a repro node.

maria: repro steps from support ticket:
```
curl -v --connect-timeout 5 --max-time 10 https://api.redwood-inference.eu/foo -o /dev/null -w "%{time_connect} %{time_appconnect} %{time_starttransfer}\n"
# returns: 0.080 3.512 3.820 (on affected runs)
```

eli: traceroute from eu-west POP ->
```
traceroute to api.redwood-inference.eu (198.51.100.12), 30 hops max, 60 byte packets
 1  10.0.1.1  0.5 ms  0.4 ms  0.4 ms
 2  198.51.100.1  1.2 ms  1.3 ms  1.1 ms
 3  198.51.100.5  3500 ms  *  3400 ms
 4  198.51.100.12  3505 ms  3408 ms  3510 ms
```
shows a 3.4s hop in path.

jonah: That smells like a blackholed path or upstream queuing causing TLS handshake stall. Could be a cross-AZ hop causing hairpin and queueing.

maria: Any config changes we can do quick? Can we force traffic to eu-west-2 POPs while this is investigated? Temporary steering to second POP set might mitigate.

eli: We can adjust anycast origin weights to lower preference for the affected POPs. Doing a quick health-check-based shift: run `edgectl route update --region eu-west --deprioritize POP-E1,POP-E3`

jonah: Also add fallback at the load balancer for TLS handshake timeout to 1.5s for affected routes so clients fail faster (helps degrade gracefully).

maria: I'm going to open a support advisory with customers impacted and note we're rerouting. Tony, pls post update in ticket thread.

tony_support: Posted to tickets 4539/4540/4542 with ETA ~10m for mitigation. Customers asked for any repro they can run; gave them the curl snippet.

eli: Executing weight change now. Command: `edgectl adjust-weight --pop POP-E1 --weight 10 && edgectl adjust-weight --pop POP-E3 --weight 10` (we reduce from 100 to 10).

deploy-bot: edgectl job queued -> job-9472, started 08:28:10 UTC.

net-bot: BGP sessions stabilized at 08:30:05, no more flaps.

jonah: after weight shift, p95 down to ~260ms, p99 ~1.1s. Improvement but not fully normal. Some residual long hops remain for a subset.

eli: digging into flow logs — affected upstream ASN 64520 shows increased queue lengths during flap window. Looks like traffic was transiently attracted to a suboptimal path (long cross-az bounce).

maria: Can we add a temporary route-level clamp: prefer eu-west-2 for any requests where TLS handshake > 2s? I know our smart routing supports latency-based routing policy.

eli: I can add a routing rule: if measured TLS handshake > 1500ms and customer tier != enterprise then route to fallback POPs in eu-west-2. Applying now. `routectl policy add --name tls-latency-fallback --threshold 1500 --action fallback:eu-west-2`

deploy-bot: policy deploy job-9475 started 08:35:14 UTC -> completed 08:35:42 UTC.

jonah: After policy, monitored p99 across affected customers ~550ms. Good.

maria: Alerts back to normal baseline at 08:42. Marking mitigations: anycast weight reduction + tls-latency-fallback policy.

eli: Root cause: upstream BGP session instability causing transient route shifts to a path with an overloaded hop in partner network, leading to large TLS handshake tail latency. Added follow-ups: 1) request partner to investigate their hop queueing, 2) add automated detection to apply fallback policy when TLS handshake tail breaches, 3) create a runbook for anycast weight adjustment.

jonah: I'll draft a short postmortem and link support tickets + graphs. Can someone capture exact times and metric links?

maria: I'll export the dashboards and attach in postmortem. Also adding runbook steps for step-by-step weight adjust and policy rollback.

tony_support: Customers notified; two asked for timeline and whether retries would help — advised that retries are likely to hit fallback after mitigation, but recommended exponential backoff.

eli: Follow-up tasks assigned: ENG-1298 partner NOC investigation, SRE-842 runbook + automation for auto-fallback, INFRA-501 add observability for hop-level TLS handshake distribution.

maria: Closing thread when postmortem is published. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

net-bot: Note: keep monitoring for 24h for recurrence.

jonah: Quick note — we should add a synthetic that does full TCP+TLS handshake timers every minute from eu-west POPs to catch these earlier. Adding that to INFRA-501.

maria: Agreed.

eli: End of thread.
